meanings.note: Habitually or in general. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to take', paired with 'взять'.
'брать' alone often means this, in talk about officials

examples.trans: We have to take all the money.

meanings.note: Polite (вы) or plural. Core Russian det meaning 'your, yours (polite or plural)' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Arkady Borisovich, who are your rivals?

meanings.note: The neuter form 'всё' used alone. Core Russian det meaning 'all, whole; everyone, everything' in everyday speech.
Neuter всё. Core Russian det meaning 'all, whole; everyone, everything' in everyday speech.
Plural все. Core Russian det meaning 'all, whole; everyone, everything' in everyday speech.
Pointing at something. Core Russian part meaning 'here, there (pointing)' in everyday speech.
Emphasis. Core Russian part meaning 'here, there (pointing)' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: All right, here you go. There, look.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'everything', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Я знаю всё в моём отеле.
examples.trans: I know everything in my hotel.

meanings.note: emphatic at the start of a sentence
Disbelief. Core Russian part meaning 'yes' in everyday speech.
давай + 1st person plural or infinitive
давай + 1st person plural or infinitive

examples.text: Давай мы его уволим, а тебя на его место назначим.
examples.trans: Let's fire him and put you in his place.

meanings.note: на днях = in the next few days, or the other day

examples.trans: I'll call in the next few days.
Any day now, on the website.

meanings.note: + genitive. Core Russian prep meaning 'until, before; up to' in everyday speech.
Core Russian prep meaning 'until, before; up to' in everyday speech.

related.gloss: to reach, walk as far as

examples.text: Позвони мне вечером. Договоримся на завтра.
examples.trans: Call me this evening. We'll arrange something for tomorrow.

meanings.note: From замечательный. Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Так это замечательно! Раньше вы чувствовали ко мне отвращение.
examples.trans: Well, that is wonderful! Before, you felt disgust toward me.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'merit, credit' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Это заслуга моих коров и свиней.
examples.trans: Is thanks to my cows and pigs.

examples.text: На нашей кухне уже есть новая заслуга.
examples.trans: In our kitchen there is already a new merit.

meanings.note: In one direction, now. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to go (on foot)', paired with 'пойти'.
To run for a second term. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to go (on foot)', paired with 'пойти'.

examples.trans: He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: From or relating to China. Relational adjective formed with the Slavic suffix '-ский' ('pertaining to'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('Chinese').

examples.text: Зачем ты эти китайские стулья таскаешь?
examples.trans: Why are you dragging these Chinese chairs around?

examples.text: Ты зачем эти китайские стулья с собой таскаешь, Даня?
examples.trans: Why are you dragging these Chinese chairs around with you, Danya?

meanings.note: Уже месяц = for a month now. Common masculine noun meaning 'month' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: I've been living here for a month.
The election is in a month.

examples.text: Мы с Пашей вместе уже месяц.
examples.trans: Pasha and I have been together for a month now.

meanings.note: нас = us (gen/acc/prep); у нас = we have, at our place

meanings.en: other forms: нас (gen/acc), нам (dat), нами (instr), нас (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'we' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!

meanings.note: Stronger contrast than 'а'. Core Russian conj meaning 'but' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо ещё.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need more.
I want to, but I can't.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо сделать ещё больше.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need to do even more.

meanings.note: hesitation, at the start of a sentence
Ну, папа!. Core Russian part meaning 'well; come on' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'vacation, leave' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Я в отпуске-то всего два раза был.
examples.trans: I have only been on vacation twice in my whole life.

examples.text: На нашей кухне уже есть новый отпуск.
examples.trans: In our kitchen there is already a new vacation.

meanings.note: Authorized or recognized. Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('official').

examples.trans: This is an official document, by the way.

examples.text: Это официальные документы о нашем разводе.
examples.trans: These are official documents regarding our divorce.

examples.text: Я тоже подам официальный рапорт об отставке.
examples.trans: I will also submit an official resignation report.

meanings.note: Prefix 'пере-' denotes crossing over, repeating, or exceeding a limit (stem 'думать'). Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to change one's mind', paired with 'передумывать'.

examples.trans: If you change your mind, come back.
If you change your mind, come back. The job is waiting.

поделить.gloss: to divide, to split, to share out

meanings.en: to divide up, to split, to share between
meanings.note: Share out between people. Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to divide, to split, to share out', paired with 'делить'.

получиться.gloss: to turn out, to work out

meanings.en: to turn out, to work out
meanings.note: Всё получилось = it all worked out. Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to turn out, to work out', paired with 'получаться'.

meanings.en: to come out of, to make
meanings.note: из тебя получится мэр = you'll make a mayor

examples.text: Классный из тебя мэр получится, Самсон.
examples.trans: You'll make a great mayor, Samson.

meanings.note: Agentive or instrument masculine noun meaning 'Monday', declining across all six Russian grammatical cases.

examples.text: В понедельник я к тебе перееду.
examples.trans: On Monday I will move in with you.

meanings.note: Verbal action or result neuter noun formed with '-ение'/'-ание', meaning 'warning' in conversational and formal Russian.

examples.trans: A warning sign is hanging here.

examples.text: Тогда вы получили бы простое предупреждение.
examples.trans: Then you would have received a simple warning.

meanings.note: The г sounds like в.

examples.text: Виктор Степанович, сегодня никак не могу.
examples.trans: Viktor Stepanovich, I really can't today.

считать.gloss: to count; to think, to consider

meanings.note: посчитать / сосчитать are the perfectives
Я считаю, что... = I think that. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to count; to think, to consider', paired with 'посчитать'.

examples.text: Эх, Паша, Паша. Ты считать не умеешь.
examples.trans: Oh, Pasha, Pasha. You can't count.

meanings.note: Direction. Core Russian adv meaning 'here (to this place)' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: The white one? Give me the keys.

meanings.note: At the start of a question. Core Russian part meaning 'so, then; like that' in everyday speech.
Core Russian part meaning 'so, then; like that' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: So I shouldn't wait for you?
So I shouldn't wait for you tonight?

meanings.note: To someone you call ты. Core Russian det meaning 'your (informal)' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Я бы на твоём месте подумал.
examples.trans: If I were you, I'd think about it.

meanings.note: in weight, or тяжёлый металл = heavy metal
Тяжёлый день = a hard day. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('heavy; hard, difficult').

examples.text: Я вообще в школе тяжёлый металл любила!
examples.trans: In school I actually loved heavy metal!

meanings.en: to leave on foot, go away
meanings.note: Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to leave, go away', paired with 'уходить'.
Declinable plural-only noun meaning 'tips', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.
+ accusative: через неделю = in a week
Core Russian prep meaning 'in (time); through' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Нормально? Она через неделю снова потечёт!
examples.trans: Fine? It'll be leaking again in a week!

meanings.note: Question word. Core Russian pron meaning 'what' in everyday speech.
Conjunction. Core Russian pron meaning 'what' in everyday speech.
Core Russian pron meaning 'what' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: Informal. Borrowed from French 'chef' (head, leader, from Latin 'caput'); in Russian kitchen culture 'шеф' is the standard form of address for the executive head chef.

examples.trans: The chef is in the kitchen.

meanings.note: pointing at a thing or a situation; 'это' + noun = 'this is ...'
points at something: это моё = that's mine
Linking word: главное — это народ. Core Russian pron meaning 'this, that; it is' in everyday speech.

meanings.en: other forms: этого, этому, это, этим, этом
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'this, that; it is' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: And this is for you. A toy car!

meanings.note: alone: 'я этого не хочу' = I don't want that

examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat.

examples.text: Меня уже тошнит от этой коммуналки! У нас труба уже неделю течёт.
examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat! Our pipe has been leaking for a week now.

meanings.note: меня = me (genitive/accusative), мне = to me (dative)

meanings.en: other forms: меня (gen/acc), мне (dat), мной (instr), мне (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'I' in everyday speech.
